tools.description: Use this when the user wants aggregate statistics over logs (counts, rates, averages, percentiles, or grouped/top-N breakdowns) rather than individual log records. Use signoz_search_logs for log rows and message inspection; use signoz_execute_builder_query only for queries this tool cannot express. Log fields are workspace-specific, so read signoz://logs/query-builder-guide and discover unfamiliar keys with signoz_get_field_keys. Defaults to the last 1 hour.

aggregations.description: Aggregation expressions to compute, written as the Query Builder writes them: count(), count_distinct(user_id), avg(duration), sum(bytes), min(x), max(x), p50(x) to p99(x), rate(), or a conditional such as countIf(severity_text = 'ERROR'). One expression or an array; results come back as __result_0, __result_1, ... in that order. Example: ["count()", "p99(duration)"]. SigNoz validates the expressions.

end.description: End time in unix milliseconds (optional). When both start and end are provided, they override timeRange.

filter.description: Filter expression text in SigNoz search syntax, not {"expression": ...} (see signoz://logs/query-builder-guide). Combine conditions with AND, OR, and parentheses. An unknown key may not fail: no rows plus a `key ... not found in metadata` warning means the key is absent. Ambiguous keys default to resource; prefix attribute.<key> or resource.<key> to choose. Log keys are workspace-specific; even service.name exists only when the log pipeline sets it. Discover keys and values with signoz_get_field_keys and signoz_get_field_values first. For message text use body CONTAINS 'term'. Only when you don't know which field holds a term, use search('term') for every field or search('term', attribute); scopes (body, attribute, resource, log) are ORed. search() is slow and may be rejected over wide time ranges. There is no key:value, STARTS WITH, or IS NULL; use LIKE 'prefix%', and EXISTS or NOT EXISTS. Example: "service.name = 'payment-svc' AND severity_text = 'ERROR'". Combined with service/severity params using AND.

functions.description: Post-query transforms applied in order to each time_series result, as an array of {name, args} objects, or a JSON-encoded string of that array. SigNoz applies them to time_series results only and returns scalar results unchanged, so set requestType to time_series. Names are the Query Builder function names, for example cutOffMin, cutOffMax, clampMin, clampMax, absolute, runningDiff, cumulativeSum, ewma3, median5, timeShift, or fillZero; args carries the function's parameters, for example [{"value": 10}] for cutOffMin. SigNoz validates names and args.

args.description: The function arguments; which ones are required depends on the function, for example a threshold for the cutOff and clamp functions.

name.description: The argument name for functions that take named arguments, such as z_score_threshold or seasonality for anomaly.

value.description: The argument value as a number, string or boolean, for example the threshold for cutOffMin or the duration for timeShift.

name.description: The function to apply, such as cutOffMin, cutOffMax, clampMin, clampMax, absolute, runningDiff, log2, log10, cumulativeSum, ewma3, ewma5, ewma7, median3, median5, median7, timeShift, anomaly or fillZero.

groupBy.description: Field names to group results by, as an array or a comma-separated string (e.g. ["service.name", "severity_text"] or 'service.name, severity_text'). Leave empty for a single aggregate value. Group by keys signoz_get_field_keys returns; an unknown key can come back as one empty group. A body field (body.<path>) can be grouped only when signoz_get_field_keys(signal="logs", fieldContext="body") lists it; otherwise SigNoz rejects it with `can be filtered but not selected or grouped` or `field not found`, so filter on it instead.

having.description: Condition on the aggregation results, in the filter syntax, applied after grouping. Reference an aggregation by its expression, for example "count() > 100" or "p99(duration_nano) > 500000000". SigNoz validates it.

limit.description: Maximum number of groups to return (default: 100, max: 10000; higher values are clamped). For time_series queries, groups are ranked across the entire time range, so a short-lived spike can fall outside the selected top groups.

orderBy.description: How to order results, as '<expression> <direction>'. The expression must be one of this call's aggregations written exactly as in aggregations, or a groupBy key, e.g. 'count_distinct(trace_id) desc' when aggregations is 'count_distinct(trace_id)', or 'service.name asc'. Omit it to sort by the first aggregation, descending.

requestType.description: Result shape. "scalar" (default) returns one value or a grouped/ranked table over the full time range; use it for totals, percentiles, and top lists. "time_series" returns time-bucketed values, with one series per group when grouped; use it for spikes, trends, changes over time, or questions about when something happened.

service.description: Shortcut filter for service name. Equivalent to adding service.name = '<value>' to filter. When this workspace's logs lack service.name, the call usually returns no rows with a `key service.name not found in metadata` warning instead of failing; discover keys with signoz_get_field_keys(signal="logs", fieldContext="resource") and filter on an available key instead.

severity.description: Shortcut filter for severity_text, matched in any case and as a prefix, so WARN also matches warning and Warning; pass the short form (ERR, WARN, INFO). Common values include DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR, and FATAL, but they are not an exhaustive enum. Discover the workspace's values with signoz_get_field_values(signal="logs", name="severity_text", fieldContext="log").

stepInterval.description: Time bucket size in seconds for time_series mode (optional). When omitted, the backend auto-selects an appropriate interval. Only set this if the user explicitly requests a specific granularity. Examples: '60' (1 min), '3600' (1 hour), '86400' (1 day).

timeRange.description: Relative time range. Format: <number><unit> where unit is 'm' (minutes), 'h' (hours), or 'd' (days). Examples: '30m', '1h', '2h', '6h', '24h', '3d', '7d'. Ignored when both start and end are provided. Defaults to '1h'.

Use signoz_search_traces for raw spans, trace-ID discovery, or one row per trace (such as the most expensive AI traces), and signoz_get_trace_details for one known trace ID. Before calling, read signoz://traces/query-builder-guide; discover unfamiliar workspace fields with signoz_get_field_keys. For the user's LLM, AI agent, token, cost, model, tool-call, or prompt questions (AI observability), set queryType to builder_ai_query and read signoz://ai/query-builder-guide. Defaults to the last 1 hour.

aggregations.description: Aggregation expressions to compute, written as the Query Builder writes them: count(), count_distinct(name), avg(duration_nano), sum(x), min(x), max(x), p50(duration_nano) to p99(duration_nano), rate(), or a conditional such as countIf(has_error = true). duration_nano is span latency in nanoseconds. One expression or an array; results come back as __result_0, __result_1, ... in that order. Example: ["count()", "p99(duration_nano)"]. SigNoz validates the expressions.

end.description: End time in unix milliseconds (optional). When both start and end are provided, they override timeRange.

error.description: Shortcut filter for error spans (true or false). Equivalent to adding has_error = true/false to filter.

filter.description: Filter expression text in SigNoz search syntax, not {"expression": ...} (see signoz://traces/query-builder-guide). search() is logs-only; traces use field predicates. Combine conditions with AND, OR, and parentheses for precedence. An unknown key may not fail: SigNoz can match a guessed attribute and return a `key ... not found in metadata` warning with no rows, so read that warning as an absent key. Keys present in multiple contexts default to resource context; disambiguate with attribute.<key>, resource.<key>, or span.<key>. Every condition needs a key and an operator: there is no full-text search, key:value, STARTS WITH, or IS NULL; use LIKE 'prefix%' and EXISTS or NOT EXISTS. Discover valid keys with signoz_get_field_keys, then confirm values with signoz_get_field_values, before filtering. Examples: "service.name = 'payment-svc' AND has_error = true", "http_method = 'POST' AND (has_error = true OR duration_nano > 1000000000)". Combined with service/operation/error/duration params using AND.

maxDuration.description: Maximum span duration, such as '500ms' or '2s' (units ns, us, ms, s, m, h). A bare number is nanoseconds: 500 means 500ns, not 500ms.

minDuration.description: Minimum span duration, such as '500ms' or '2s' (units ns, us, ms, s, m, h). A bare number is nanoseconds: 500 means 500ns, not 500ms.

One call cannot mix trace-level and span-level aggregations; count() and count_distinct(trace_id) are span-level, so count AI traces with count_distinct(trace_id) in a separate call.

tools.description: Use this when the user wants a new SigNoz alert rule; use signoz_update_alert to change an existing rule. Supports v2alpha1 threshold, PromQL, and metric anomaly alerts. Read signoz://alert/instructions and signoz://alert/examples before composing any payload, unless already read in the same prepared operation; for PromQL also read signoz://promql/instructions. For direct routing, reuse a fully paginated signoz_list_notification_channels result only from the same still-current prepared operation; otherwise call it, refreshing only if state may have changed. Use exact returned immutable routing displayName values, not machine name. If none fits, ask the user or offer signoz_create_notification_channel with settings the user provides; never guess or create automatically. SigNoz rejects a threshold tier with no channels or an unknown channel name; confirmed v2 policy routing may omit tier channels. Top-level preferredChannels plays no part in routing.

alert.description: The display name of the alert rule.

alertType.description: The signal the rule evaluates: METRIC_BASED_ALERT, TRACES_BASED_ALERT, LOGS_BASED_ALERT, EXCEPTIONS_BASED_ALERT or AI_TRACES_BASED_ALERT.

annotations.description: Free text attached to every alert, conventionally summary and description. Values may use Go templates with $value, $threshold and $labels.

condition.description: The query to evaluate and the thresholds applied to its result.

absentFor.description: How many minutes without data pass before the nodata alert fires. Ignored unless alertOnAbsent is true.

alertOnAbsent.description: Whether to fire a nodata alert when the query returns no data. Defaults to false.

algorithm.description: anomaly_rule only: the anomaly detection algorithm. The supported value is standard.

compositeQuery.description: The queries whose result is compared against the thresholds.

panelType.description: The panel the UI renders the queries with: graph, table or value. Use graph for alerts.

queries.description: The queries to evaluate, at least one. Every envelope type must match queryType: builder_query and builder_formula for builder, promql for promql, clickhouse_sql for clickhouse_sql.

queryType.description: The query language of every query: builder, promql or clickhouse_sql.

unit.description: The unit of the query result, such as percent, ms or bytes. Used to format values in notifications and to convert thresholds given in a different targetUnit.

matchType.description: schemaVersion v1 only: which points in the window must satisfy op. Accepted as at_least_once, all_the_times, on_average, in_total or last, their aliases avg and sum, or the legacy codes as strings, '1' to '5'. Required for v1; v2alpha1 sets matchType on each threshold.

op.description: schemaVersion v1 only: how the value is compared with target. Accepted as above, below, equal, not_equal, above_or_equal, below_or_equal or outside_bounds, their symbols, or the legacy codes as strings, '1' to '7'. Required for v1; v2alpha1 sets op on each threshold.

requireMinPoints.description: Whether a series is skipped until it has at least requiredNumPoints points in the window. Defaults to false.

requiredNumPoints.description: The minimum number of points a series needs before it is evaluated. Must be greater than 0 when requireMinPoints is true.

seasonality.description: anomaly_rule only: the seasonal period the history is compared against, hourly, daily or weekly.

selectedQueryName.description: The name of the query whose result is evaluated, such as A or F1. Must match a query in compositeQuery.

target.description: schemaVersion v1 only: the value compared against, in targetUnit. Required for v1; v2alpha1 sets target on each threshold.

targetUnit.description: schemaVersion v1 only: the unit of target, such as percent or ms. Converted to compositeQuery.unit before comparison when the two differ.

thresholds.description: The thresholds to evaluate, as a kind and spec.

description.description: A human readable description of what the rule monitors.

disabled.description: Whether the rule is paused. A disabled rule is neither evaluated nor notifies. Defaults to false.

evalWindow.description: The lookback window as a Go duration such as 5m. Only read when schemaVersion is v1, defaulting to 5m; v2alpha1 rules set it in evaluation.spec instead.

evaluation.description: The evaluation window, as a kind and spec.

frequency.description: How often the rule is evaluated, as a Go duration such as 1m. Only read when schemaVersion is v1, defaulting to 1m; v2alpha1 rules set it in evaluation.spec instead.

labels.description: Labels attached to every alert the rule fires. Keys match [a-zA-Z_.][a-zA-Z0-9_.]*; values may use Go templates such as {{$labels.service_name}}. severity is the conventional routing label.

groupBy.description: Label names whose values group alerts into one notification, such as service.name.

newGroupEvalDelay.description: A grace period, as a Go duration such as 2m, during which a newly seen label group is excluded from evaluation. Applies to metric rules only; log and trace rules are never delayed. A group whose values are not yet known is evaluated immediately.

renotify.description: Whether and how often to re-send a notification for an alert that stays active.

alertStates.description: The alert states that are re-notified: firing, nodata or both.

enabled.description: Whether an active alert is re-sent after interval elapses. When false an alert notifies once per firing.

interval.description: The time between repeat notifications, as a Go duration such as 4h. Must be positive when enabled is true.

usePolicy.description: When true, alerts are routed by the organisation level notification policies instead of the channels named on the thresholds. Defaults to false.

preferredChannels.description: The displayName of each notification channel to notify, for schemaVersion v1 rules. Ignored for v2alpha1, where each threshold carries its own channels.

ruleType.description: The evaluation strategy: threshold_rule compares against thresholds, promql_rule evaluates a PromQL expression, anomaly_rule scores deviation from seasonal history. Defaults to threshold_rule for builder and clickhouse_sql queries and is forced to promql_rule for promql queries.

source.description: The URL of the page the rule was created from. Informational; it is not used for evaluation.

version.description: The query payload version. Nothing reads it.

isMonotonic.description: Whether a sum metric only increases. Auto-fetched when metricType is omitted.

metricType.description: gauge, sum, histogram, exponential_histogram, or summary. Omit to auto-fetch it with temporality and monotonicity.

temporality.description: cumulative, delta, or unspecified. Auto-fetched when metricType is omitted.

Names are the Query Builder function names, for example cutOffMin, cutOffMax, clampMin, clampMax, absolute, runningDiff, cumulativeSum, ewma3, median5, timeShift, or fillZero; args carries the function's parameters, for example [{"value": 10}] for cutOffMin. value.description: The argument value as a number, string or boolean, for example the threshold for cutOffMin or the duration for timeShift.

name.description: The function to apply, such as cutOffMin, cutOffMax, clampMin, clampMax, absolute, runningDiff, log2, log10, cumulativeSum, ewma3, ewma5, ewma7, median3, median5, median7, timeShift, anomaly or fillZero.

tools.description: Use this when the user wants individual log records or messages matching text, service, severity, or field filters. It returns paginated rows, not counts, trends, or grouped breakdowns; use signoz_aggregate_logs for those, and signoz_execute_builder_query only for queries this tool cannot express. Rows carry a default set of log columns; to include other attributes, such as service.name, name them in selectFields. A field missing from a row was not selected. You do not need the guide when using only searchText, service, severity, time, or pagination. Read signoz://logs/query-builder-guide before filtering on unfamiliar fields. Defaults to the last 1 hour.

filter.description: Filter expression text in SigNoz search syntax, not {"expression": ...} (see signoz://logs/query-builder-guide). Combine conditions with AND, OR, and parentheses. An unknown key may not fail: no rows plus a `key ... not found in metadata` warning means the key is absent. Ambiguous keys default to resource; prefix attribute.<key> or resource.<key> to choose. Log keys are workspace-specific; even service.name exists only when the log pipeline sets it. Discover keys and values with signoz_get_field_keys and signoz_get_field_values first. For message text use body CONTAINS 'term'. Only when you don't know which field holds a term, use search('term') for every field or search('term', attribute); scopes (body, attribute, resource, log) are ORed. search() is slow and may be rejected over wide time ranges. There is no key:value, STARTS WITH, or IS NULL; use LIKE 'prefix%', and EXISTS or NOT EXISTS. Example: "service.name = 'payment-svc' AND severity_text = 'ERROR'".

Scopes other than body are slower, and SigNoz may reject them over wide time ranges. Use them only when you don't know which key holds the text; when you do, put a predicate such as attribute.<key> CONTAINS 'text' in filter instead. Ignored, with a note, when searchText is empty.

searchText.description: Literal text to find, escaped automatically. searchScope chooses where it matches; the default is the log body. Combines with filter using AND.

tools.description: Use this when the user wants individual span rows matching service, operation, error, duration, or field filters, needs to discover trace IDs, or wants one row per trace (requestType=trace), such as the slowest traces or the most expensive AI traces. It returns paginated rows, not aggregate trends/groups or a full trace hierarchy; use signoz_aggregate_traces for statistics and signoz_get_trace_details for one known trace ID. Span rows carry a default set of span fields; name other fields in selectFields. A field missing from a row was not selected, so do not read it as absent from the span. Read signoz://traces/query-builder-guide before using unfamiliar workspace fields. For the user's LLM, AI agent, token, cost, model, tool-call, or prompt questions (AI observability), set queryType to builder_ai_query and read signoz://ai/query-builder-guide. filter.description: Filter expression text in SigNoz search syntax, not {"expression": ...} (see signoz://traces/query-builder-guide). search() is logs-only; traces use field predicates. Combine conditions with AND, OR, and parentheses for precedence. An unknown key may not fail: SigNoz can match a guessed attribute and return a `key ... not found in metadata` warning with no rows, so read that warning as an absent key. Keys present in multiple contexts default to resource context; disambiguate with attribute.<key>, resource.<key>, or span.<key>. Every condition needs a key and an operator: there is no full-text search, key:value, STARTS WITH, or IS NULL; use LIKE 'prefix%' and EXISTS or NOT EXISTS. Discover valid keys with signoz_get_field_keys, then confirm values with signoz_get_field_values, before filtering. Examples: "service.name = 'payment-svc' AND has_error = true", "http_method = 'POST' AND (has_error = true OR duration_nano > 1000000000)". Combined with shortcut params using AND.

tools.description: Use this when the user wants to replace one notification channel's complete config: {kind, spec}; it is a full replacement and may change the provider kind. First call signoz_get_notification_channel and preserve every setting the user did not ask to change; send only id and config, because name and displayName are immutable. A fetched config is writable as-is; to unset an optional field, omit it, because SigNoz rejects an empty string for template-backed fields such as titles and messages. SigNoz also rejects an unknown kind and an unknown or missing spec field with the exact requirement; signoz://notification-channel/examples lists every kind's spec fields.
